summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 11, part 55) follows Rebecca, a girl who feels guilty about missing a Sunday-school concert, which left two younger children unprompted and the class unprepared for a difficult Scripture reading. As self-punishment she throws her beloved pink parasol down the well, believing she is making a sacrifice like the heathen mothers casting babies to crocodiles. The next morning, after she has gone to school, the parasol's ivory hook catches in the well's chain gear, and Abijah Flagg is called to retrieve it, leaving the water-drawing problem unresolved in the excerpt's final line.
one_line: Rebecca throws her pink parasol down a well as self-punishment for skipping a Sunday-school concert, and it jams the well's chain gear.
key_facts: Rebecca stayed home from the Sunday-school concert, a function she was extremely fond of.
Two infants who relied on Rebecca to prompt them broke down ignominiously at the concert because of her absence.
The class had to read a difficult chapter of Scripture in rotation, and the names of the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Perizzites fell to the least capable members.
Rebecca decided that self-punishment must begin at home and chose to give up her beloved pink parasol.
Rebecca flung the pink parasol into the well, after feeling one unresigned shudder at the moment of renunciation.
Rebecca compared her sacrifice to the heathen mothers who cast their babes to the crocodiles in the Ganges.
Rebecca slept well and arose refreshed after throwing the parasol down the well.
After breakfast there was great difficulty in drawing water from the well.
Rebecca had already gone to school when Abijah Flagg was summoned to deal with the well.
The ivory hook of the parasol had caught in the chain gear of the well.
When water was first drawn, the parasol was jerked up, bent, and its strong ribs jammed into the well side, entangling it.
